.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:2:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:3:On 2026-08-13 the user confirmed that the failure occurs when one provider host launches another provider through CLI mode, such as Claude invoking Codex or Codex invoking Claude. A ten-minute caller timeout can detach or terminate observation even though the provider process may still be doing useful work. The related B-1be5 proposal only considered heuristic ledger provenance and does not solve this execution failure. During B-137a PLAN scope review, the first design was formally reopened because its evidence write ordering would either deadlock before terminal or let the controller impersonate the reviewer.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:4:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:5:## Key Insights
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:6:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:7:The framework must supervise the provider process at the actual execution boundary. A worker heartbeat and provider progress are different facts; output silence is diagnostic rather than terminal. Every wait must be bounded, every run must have a finite absolute deadline, and a durable next-touch reconciler must be able to materialize terminal truth even when the original worker becomes wedged. Formal reviewer evidence must bind to the exact managed receipt instead of provider plus story plus time-window guesses.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:8:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:9:Reviewer evidence also needs a two-phase provenance protocol. The provider reviewer authors an immutable proposal containing its pass/findings and truthful read evidence while the run is active. It cannot call the final evidence writer before the terminal receipt and evidence journal are sealed. After successful terminal, a mechanical importer validates the sealed proposal and imports it without allowing the controller to change the verdict or become the reviewer. The new composite evidence class must use the existing shared Proof Admissibility artifact registry, intake, reason vocabulary and evaluator at both write-time and REVIEW-gate consumption; a parallel special-case proof system is not acceptable.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:10:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:11:## Solution Tradeoffs
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:12:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:13:A single deep ManagedHostRun module adds durable runtime artifacts, worker continuation and reconciliation complexity, but removes duplicated foreground/background supervision and makes cancellation, cleanup and evidence semantics consistent. M1 execution safety and M2 gate evidence ship together so the framework does not claim enforcement while raw CLI reviews can still satisfy formal gates. The two-phase proposal/import protocol adds one post-terminal mechanical step, but preserves the actual provider reviewer as evidence author and prevents controller self-absolution. Reusing shared Proof Admissibility adds registry work but avoids a second trust vocabulary and keeps gate-consumed facts centrally auditable. Legacy configured provider timeout ceilings remain separate and unchanged.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:14:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:15:## Conversational Texture
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:16:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/background.md:17:The user repeatedly emphasized that a ten-minute boundary must not cause an automatic restart, that silent but still-running agents should continue to be monitored, and that the target is host-independent cross-provider CLI execution rather than native subagent APIs. After iterative Claude Opus review and empirical Codex/POSIX probes, the user approved the consolidated design and explicitly asked to start a Story and implement it. The user values a framework-level solution at the provider CLI boundary: bounded observation, no duplicate restart, honest terminal/cancel truth, and proof that the exact provider review—not a controller-authored substitute—satisfied the formal gate.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:1:# B-137a implementation plan
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:2:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:3:## Public seams and invariant order
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:4:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:5:The behavior-facing seams are:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:6:1. `host_run` submit/foreground attach;
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:7:2. `host_run_status(runId, waitMs<=30000)`;
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:8:3. `host_run_cancel(runId, reason?)`;
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:9:4. `cross_host_review` as the privileged verdict-profile owner;
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:10:5. `review_pass_set` / `finding_add` plus the REVIEW gate as managed-evidence consumers.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:11:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:12:Private worker, file layout, launch adapters and reconciliation helpers are tested only through those seams or through real child-process effects. Each vertical slice follows RED → minimal GREEN; implementation does not bulk-create imagined internal tests.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:13:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:14:## CHK-001 — Persist and reconcile managed host-run lifecycle
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:15:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:16:Create a deep `core/managed-host-run.ts` module whose small interface owns submit, attach/status projection, cancel, worker execution and reconcile. A run gets a generated `hrun_*` identity and an immutable root under `.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:17:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:18:Submit writes immutable/spec-bound state atomically: `spec.json`, digest-only `owner.json`, 0600 one-shot `input.cap` and `input.prompt`, initial `snapshot.json`, and append-only `events.jsonl`. The hidden worker wins `claim.json` using exclusive create, validates the one-shot capability, unlinks both input files, marks `claimReady`, acquires provider admission, launches the private provider adapter and periodically advances `workerHeartbeatAt`. Provider output updates a separate `lastProviderProgressAt` only when observable; unsupported observability is represented as `unobservable`, never fabricated.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:19:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:20:A terminal is created exclusively and exactly once. It records outcome, timing, exit/timeout/cancel reason, provider identity, spec/profile binding digests, evidence journal digest, process cleanup facts, residual process state and an independent `replacementSafe`. Repeated status/cancel/attach calls first acquire a short `reconcile.lock`, re-read facts, and materialize terminal truth for deadline expiry or authoritative worker/provider death. Silence is never a transition predicate. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity yields honest residual `unknown` and `replacementSafe:false`, not blind termination.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:21:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:22:Initial RED tests cover: exclusive claim winner, unchanged running state across silent intervals, worker crash followed by deadline reconciliation, one terminal under concurrent reconcilers, idempotent status/cancel, terminal/result digest stability, capability/prompt deletion, and no automatic retry.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:23:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:24:## CHK-002 — Expose submit, attach, status and cancel command surfaces
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:25:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:26:Extend the host-run command schema:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:27:- `host_run --detach` submits, waits only for a bounded claim handshake, and returns `runId/state/deadlineAt/generation`;
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:28:- foreground `host_run` calls the same submit path then attaches to that run, projecting live output and final usage without owning the provider child;
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:29:- `host_run_status --runId ... --waitMs ...` performs bounded long-poll, returning immediately on terminal or snapshot-generation change and otherwise after at most 30000ms;
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:30:- `host_run_cancel --runId ... --reason ...` writes an idempotent cooperative request and reconciles;
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:31:- hidden `host_run_worker --runId ...` is runtime-only and never advertised as an operator workflow.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:32:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:33:Declare command policy, process-fact level and CLI watchdog behavior for runtime continuation. A foreground caller/watchdog exit may end attachment but cannot convert the managed run to failed or cancel the worker. JSON stdout remains one machine object; text mode keeps live stream routing and concise status guidance. The handler never stores raw prompt/capability in argv or durable public artifacts.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:34:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:35:RED starts at CLI/handler seams: detach returns after claim, status wait is capped, foreground and detached share one run/receipt shape, cancel is idempotent, unknown run is fail-closed, and caller termination leaves the run queryable.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:36:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:37:## CHK-003 — Supervise provider processes portably and honestly
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:38:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:39:Provider adapters remain private to ManagedHostRun and preserve canonical launcher specifications. Codex uses documented `codex exec ... -`, the worker writes the prompt to stdin and closes it. Claude retains its canonical launcher contract. Agy is unavailable for ManagedHostRun because its current print launcher accepts the prompt only in argv, so managed execution refuses it before provider spawn until a stdin or protected prompt-file transport exists.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:40:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:41:On POSIX, spawn the provider as a new process group and persist PID/PGID plus a launch fingerprint. Cancellation/deadline cleanup is TERM → bounded grace → KILL → reap → residual probe. Identity is revalidated before signals. On unsupported platforms, managed execution refuses before provider spawn with a structured unsupported-platform terminal; it does not silently degrade to child-only cleanup.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:42:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:43:Move the first-output clock to diagnostics only. Preserve finite total timeout/deadline, bounded output projection, provider usage candidate extraction, turn-failure diagnostic, passthrough-degradation honesty and failure classification. Worker heartbeat and provider progress are distinct fields.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:44:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:45:RED uses real local Node subprocesses for silent completion, descendant cleanup and TERM-resistant escalation, plus injected provider adapters for Codex argv/stdin closure, overflow and parsing.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:46:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:47:## CHK-004 — Enforce shared provider admission independent of usage-ledger mode
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:48:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:49:Extract the slot registry from the ledger-gated branch into one provider-admission module. Acquisition happens before every provider spawn regardless of `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER`; usage preflight/budget/final rows remain conditional and keep existing fail-closed/append-honesty semantics. Slot ownership token, dead-PID reclaim, corrupt-meta stale backstop and token-guarded release remain unchanged.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:50:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:51:Inventory production provider launch sites. Managed host_run and cross_host_review use ManagedHostRun admission. Direct Codex/Claude/Gemini leaves that are not managed execution are classified by the provider execution registry as `admission_only` or `adapter_only` according to their admission owner; `legacy_unmanaged` is reserved and empty by contract, and `admission_managed` is not a status. Add a source registry/contract smoke so a new direct spawn path fails review until classified.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:52:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:53:Preserve candidate-spec per-chunk streaming, 64KiB discard-all overflow and null first-output diagnostics. RED covers ledger-off cap contention, dead/corrupt/live slot reclaim, release race, and source inventory completeness.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:54:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:55:## CHK-005 — Route cross-host review through managed execution
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:56:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:57:Keep `cross_host_review` as profile owner. It still resolves the authoritative story worktree, captures clean HEAD/material/storyFiles facts, authorizes read-only Codex dispatch, creates the detached review snapshot, redacts environment, computes the existing policy timeout ceiling, constructs the structured-verdict prompt and validates the returned verdict schema.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:58:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:59:Replace only its direct provider execution with internal ManagedHostRun submit+attach using profile `cross-host-verdict` and opaque bindings. The terminal receipt is included in paired host-verdict provenance. Provider nonzero/timeout/cancel/admission refusal/invalid verdict continue to yield the existing honest blocked/error decision; no raw provider stdout becomes gate evidence.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:60:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:61:Protect configured `provider.codex`, `cross_host_review`, bounded retry and fail-closed policies with exact source/runtime regression assertions. RED captures the current direct leaf, then proves the managed path while all existing cross-host checks remain green.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:62:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:63:## CHK-006 — Bind formal reviewer evidence to exact managed receipts
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:64:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:65:Add a versioned managed-execution binding and a two-phase provider-authored evidence protocol. The profile owner seals opaque bindings at submit: storyId, reviewRunId, lane, intended provider/transport, prompt-envelope/body/context/assembled digests, materialHash, headHash and storyFilesHash. While running, the provider reviewer writes exactly one immutable proposal into the evidence journal: pass or findings plus truthful readManifest/readLog and its registered reviewer identity. It does not call final `review_pass_set` or `finding_add`.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:66:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:67:Successful terminal creation seals the spec digest, proposal digest and append-only journal digest. After terminal, `managed_review_evidence_import` accepts only a runId/receipt reference, reads the sealed provider-authored bytes, and imports the existing ReviewPass/Finding shape while preserving agent/lane/reviewRun/read provenance exactly. It exposes no verdict/note/finding override fields, is idempotent, and refuses non-success terminal, residual/replacement ambiguity, missing/multiple proposals or any digest mismatch. The controller may trigger import but cannot become the reviewer or reinterpret its verdict.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:68:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:69:Register this managed receipt/composite evidence as a canonical artifact kind in shared Proof Admissibility with producer boundary, scope, REVIEW consumer, claim kind, temporal/material role, semantic field binding and canonical reason codes. Both import-time admission and the REVIEW gate must call the same shared registry/intake/evaluator; process-fact registry declares the gate semantics but is not a substitute. The gate revalidates current terminal, proposal/journal integrity, exact ReviewRun/lane/provider/prompt envelope and current material tuple instead of trusting persisted booleans.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:70:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:71:Native-host reviewer lanes retain their existing signed ReviewRun/pass/finding path and are not falsely described as mechanically supervised by ManagedHostRun. Main/implementer/controller-authored evidence, raw CLI output, usage-ledger rows, B-1be5-style time-window matching, pre-terminal proposals and structured degraded decisions cannot upgrade to normal managed receipt assurance.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:72:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:73:RED tests the valid provider proposal → successful terminal seal → importer → REVIEW gate path, plus forged runId/terminal/journal/proposal, stale/cross-story/cross-lane/cross-provider/material mismatch, raw CLI absence, controller override/self-assertion, multiple proposals, importer replay, and non-success terminal. A mutation/source-contract test proves both write-time and gate call the shared evaluator: bypassing either call or adding a parallel special-case evaluator must fail.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:74:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:75:## CHK-007 — Add adversarial coverage, observability, migration docs and rollout controls
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:76:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:77:Create an auto-discovered aggregate smoke so no package.json script is needed. It runs focused managed lifecycle, command, real process-group, admission, cross-host and receipt-gate tests. Add bounded mutation bites that prove premature silence failure, terminal-only monitoring and forged receipt changes are caught. Avoid destructive shared-dist mutations during parallel review.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:78:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:79:Register host-run runtime artifacts with gitignore/material-hash/repair semantics. `doctor`/status diagnostics distinguish worker liveness, provider progress observability, deadline, cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. GC removes only terminal runs beyond retention; active runs and unconsumed one-shot inputs are protected, while failed startup cleanup removes secrets.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:80:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:81:Update `docs/host-run-usage.md` and add `docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md` as the durable decision truth. Document exact operator commands, 30-second wait semantics, deadline reconciliation, no silence-based restart, the `managed`/`admission_only`/`adapter_only`/`readiness_probe` registry terms, that `legacy_unmanaged` is reserved and `admission_managed` is not a status, the local same-uid trust ceiling, and that native subagents are out of scope.
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:82:
.lattice/story/actives/B-137a/plan.md:83:Rollout is compatibility-first for non-review agent runs but enforcement is immediate for the new managed CLI-review evidence class: a raw CLI execution may still be used manually, but it cannot satisfy a formal managed reviewer gate. Final verification includes build, focused aggregate smoke, existing host-run/cross-host/provider/dispatch/review/gate suites, process/runtime registry contracts, source scans, protected timeout diff, and a real caller-detach scenario whose original run reaches terminal without a duplicate.

docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:3:Status: Adopted

docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:6:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:7:## Context
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:8:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:9:When a Claude host started Codex (or a Codex host started Claude) with raw shell
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:10:execution, the caller owned the child process implicitly. A caller watchdog,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:11:terminal disconnect, or ten-minute foreground boundary could end observation
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:12:without proving that the provider had failed. Treating that loss of observation
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:13:as failure caused duplicate reviewer launches; treating `running` forever as
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:14:proof of health caused unbounded waits. Output silence alone answers neither
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:15:question.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:16:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:17:Proofbound is host-neutral. Native Codex/Claude subagent lifecycle APIs are not
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:18:portable and therefore are not the execution contract. This decision covers
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:19:only Proofbound-owned cross-provider CLI processes.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:20:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:21:## Decision
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:22:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:23:Proofbound owns every public `host_run` and every formal cross-provider CLI
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:24:reviewer launch through a durable `ManagedHostRun`. General provider workloads
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:25:such as planned steps and autopilot repair keep their existing bounded adapters
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:26:but share the mandatory provider-process admission registry; they do not claim
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:27:durable reviewer ownership or reviewer evidence. The caller submits and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:28:observes; a detached worker owns the managed provider process until an exclusive
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:29:terminal record exists.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:30:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:31:The public surface is:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:32:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:33:- `host_run`: submit, optionally attach in foreground, or return after claim
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:34:  with `--detach`;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:35:- `host_run_status`: read or long-poll one run for at most 30 seconds;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:36:- `host_run_cancel`: idempotently request cancellation;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:37:- `host_run_worker`: private runtime continuation, dispatchable internally but
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:38:  hidden from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:39:- `managed_review_proposal_set`: compatibility-only provider callback for older
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:40:  adapters, not the formal managed happy path;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:41:- `managed_review_evidence_import`: verdict-free exact-receipt importer.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:42:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:43:`cross_host_review` remains the policy/profile owner for paired host verdicts,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:44:but its Codex leaf executes inside ManagedHostRun and exposes the managed run
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:45:and receipt in host-B provenance.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:46:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:47:## State and liveness contract
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:48:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:49:The states are `submitted`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:50:`timed_out`. Exactly one terminal file wins by exclusive creation. Repeated
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:51:status, cancel and resume operations are idempotent and never create a new run.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:52:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:53:Two clocks are deliberately distinct:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:54:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:55:- `workerHeartbeatAt` shows that the supervisor can still update its durable
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:56:  snapshot;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:57:- `lastProviderProgressAt` changes only when observable provider stdout/stderr
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:58:  arrives.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:59:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:60:Neither clock is a completion oracle. A provider may legitimately be silent,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:61:and a worker heartbeat does not prove provider progress. Expiry of a 30-second
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:62:observation wait is non-terminal: it only wakes the caller and never authorizes
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:63:a retry. The `host_run_status` call is also the run's next-touch reconciler,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:64:however, so during that call an already-requested cancellation or an expired
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:65:absolute deadline can legitimately publish the corresponding `cancelled` or
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:66:`timed_out` terminal state.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:67:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:68:Every run has a finite absolute deadline (30 minutes by default, bounded to 24
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:69:hours). Deadline or cancellation reconciliation performs bounded TERM, KILL,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:70:reap and residual probing. Replacement is safe only when cleanup facts prove
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:71:there is no residual process group. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity remains
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:72:`replacementSafe=false`; it is not guessed away.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:73:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:74:## Persistence and process ownership
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:75:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:76:Each run has a 0700 directory at
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:77:`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:78:primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:79:DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:80:bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:81:capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:82:Prompt, capability and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot inputs;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:83:the worker validates and deletes them before provider launch. Only root and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:84:runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:85:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:86:On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Codex receives the
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:87:prompt through documented stdin (`codex exec ... -`). Claude receives a 0600
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:88:one-shot prompt file below the exact provider cwd's ignored
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:89:`.lattice/runtime/host-run-prompts/` tree, because Claude's workspace sandbox
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:90:rejects an otherwise protected OS-temp prompt outside that cwd. Prompt text never
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:91:enters argv and the private leaf is removed after settlement. A detached formal
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:92:Claude reviewer has no approval terminal, so only the signed `managed_reviewer`
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:93:profile launches it with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; ordinary Claude
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:94:host runs retain their configured policy, and the strict final proposal/parser
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:95:boundary is unchanged. The current agy print launcher accepts prompt text only
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:96:in argv, so managed agy execution refuses before provider spawn until agy
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:97:exposes a stdin or protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:98:likewise refuse before provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:99:is equivalent.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:100:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:101:## Shared provider admission
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:102:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:103:Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:104:of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:105:token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:106:Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:107:not process admission.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:108:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:109:A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:110:reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:111:checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:112:already been reclaimed and reassigned.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:113:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:114:Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:115:admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:116:review evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:117:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:118:### Provider execution surface classification
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:119:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:120:Every production provider spawn site is classified by
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:121:`ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus` (`packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts`),
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:122:and `packages/main/src/tasks/provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts` fails if a
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:123:new spawn path appears without one:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:124:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:125:| Status | Meaning |
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:126:|---|---|
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:127:| `managed` | Executes through ManagedHostRun: durable run identity, supervised process group, absolute deadline, exactly one terminal receipt. |
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:128:| `admission_only` | Not managed-executed, but routed through the shared provider admission boundary, so the concurrency cap and slot accounting still apply. |
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:129:| `adapter_only` | A low-level adapter module whose *caller* owns admission; the adapter itself makes no gate claim. |
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:130:| `readiness_probe` | Version/readiness probing only. Never becomes review evidence. |
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:131:| `legacy_unmanaged` | A provider spawn that is neither managed nor admission-routed. **Reserved, and currently empty by contract.** |
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:132:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:133:`admission_managed` is not a status value: admission and managed execution are
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:134:two separate properties, expressed by `admission_only` (admission without
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:135:managed execution) and `managed` (both).
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:136:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:137:The `legacy_unmanaged` bucket exists so an unmanaged spawn path must be declared
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:138:rather than pass silently. It is asserted empty — `provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts`
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:139:requires that no surface carries it — so adding one is a deliberate, reviewable
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:140:act that fails the contract until justified. It is not a claim that unmanaged
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:141:execution is impossible, only that none is currently admitted.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:142:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:143:## Formal managed reviewer evidence
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:144:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:145:Native-host reviewers retain the existing signed ReviewRun plus direct
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:146:ReviewPass/Finding flow. A cross-provider CLI reviewer uses a two-phase flow:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:147:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:148:1. The controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:149:2. `host_run --managedReview` derives the exact assembled prompt and seals
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:150:   story, provider, lane, ReviewRun, head, material, story-files and prompt
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:151:   bindings.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:152:3. The managed prompt requires the provider's final assistant result to be one
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:153:   bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope with
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:154:   pass-or-findings and truthful read evidence. It cannot write final
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:155:   `review_pass_set`/`finding_add` evidence from inside the managed run. After a
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:156:   successful provider exit, the owning adapter selects only Codex's terminal
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:157:   `item.completed` `agent_message` or Claude's successful terminal
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:158:   provider-validated `structured_output` (`type=result`, `subtype=success`,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:159:   field present). Claude non-success result events, success events without
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:160:   `structured_output`, and `event.result` are ignored. Claude's signed
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:161:   managed-review launch supplies a bounded non-secret `--json-schema` bound
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:162:   to the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple. Tool logs, arbitrary
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:163:   stdout, Claude prose or fenced JSON, and controller fields are never
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:164:   proposal inputs. The worker
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:165:   validates the same tuple and atomically writes the immutable proposal.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:166:   Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized final envelopes fail the managed
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:167:   run closed. The older descriptor-authorized
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:168:   `managed_review_proposal_set` callback remains compatibility-only.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:169:4. Successful terminal creation seals spec, proposal, result, live-output and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:170:   event-journal digests plus cleanup facts.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:171:5. The controller calls `managed_review_evidence_import` with only the exact
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:172:   runId and receiptId. It cannot provide or alter verdict bytes. Import still
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:173:   fails closed unless the completed receipt proves `replacementSafe=true`,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:174:   `processCleanup.reaped=true`, and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:175:   `processCleanup.residualProcessGroup=false`.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:176:6. The importer preserves provider reviewer/lane/ReviewRun/read provenance and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:177:   writes the existing signed ReviewPass/Finding shape.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:178:7. Import time and the REVIEW gate both call the shared Proof Admissibility
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:179:   registry/intake/evaluator and revalidate the current terminal, proposal,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:180:   journal, prompt and material tuple.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:181:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:182:Raw CLI output outside the trusted final-result adapter lane, usage-ledger rows, time-window correlations, pre-terminal
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:183:proposals, failed/cancelled/timed-out terminals and controller-authored verdicts
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:184:cannot upgrade to managed reviewer evidence. Raw same-UID CLI calls, forged
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:185:environment values, stale process groups, terminal/reaped runs and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:186:ambiguous/multiple active candidates cannot borrow the descriptor authority.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:187:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:188:The worker's reserved durable cancellation reason
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:189:`absolute_deadline_exceeded` always reconciles to a `timed_out` terminal with
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:190:that exact reason, even if the next observation occurs through the cancellation
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:191:branch. Human/operator cancellation remains `cancelled`; both paths retain the
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:192:same cleanup and replacement-safety proof.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:193:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:194:The authority classifications remain disjoint. A native-host reviewer keeps the
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:195:signed ReviewRun plus direct ReviewPass/Finding path only when a registered
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:196:host-adapter broker signs the exact closeout invocation. Its Ed25519 attestation
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:197:binds Story, agent/lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:198:adapter/host identity and a one-shot nonce. Lattice stores the registered public

docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:233:

docs/host-run-usage.md:1:# Durable managed host runs, reviewer receipts, and usage diagnostics
docs/host-run-usage.md:2:
docs/host-run-usage.md:3:Proofbound launches Codex and Claude as managed cross-provider CLI processes.
docs/host-run-usage.md:4:`lattice host_run` submits those processes to a durable
docs/host-run-usage.md:5:`ManagedHostRun`: the detached worker, not the caller shell, owns the provider
docs/host-run-usage.md:6:until a terminal record exists. A caller may attach, time out, disconnect, or
docs/host-run-usage.md:7:return after 30 seconds without cancelling or replacing the provider run.
docs/host-run-usage.md:8:
docs/host-run-usage.md:9:The same launch path records optional LLM usage diagnostics. Usage rows are not
docs/host-run-usage.md:10:the execution owner and disabling them does not disable shared provider-process
docs/host-run-usage.md:11:admission. `lattice usage_sweep` remains the read-only companion for sessions
docs/host-run-usage.md:12:that never used the managed boundary.
docs/host-run-usage.md:13:
docs/host-run-usage.md:14:## Why this exists
docs/host-run-usage.md:15:
docs/host-run-usage.md:16:A 2026-07-10 token-burn audit found the usage ledger only ever saw a handful of
docs/host-run-usage.md:17:probe rows: host-side reviewer launches, quorum cross-host reviews, and long
docs/host-run-usage.md:18:desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every
docs/host-run-usage.md:19:`host_run` receives a durable `runId`, an absolute deadline and an exclusive
docs/host-run-usage.md:20:terminal receipt. The runtime persists under the primary worktree at
docs/host-run-usage.md:21:`.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`, so Story worktree cleanup cannot erase an
docs/host-run-usage.md:22:active run or its receipt; secrets and prompt bytes are 0600
docs/host-run-usage.md:23:one-shot inputs removed when the worker claims them. Interactive desktop and
docs/host-run-usage.md:24:native-subagent lifecycles remain outside this boundary and are covered only by
docs/host-run-usage.md:25:their host or by read-only retrospective diagnostics.
docs/host-run-usage.md:26:
docs/host-run-usage.md:27:Usage rows are diagnostics only (`gateEvidence=false`). They never gate the
docs/host-run-usage.md:28:workflow, never satisfy REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority evidence, and never advance a
docs/host-run-usage.md:29:phase.
docs/host-run-usage.md:30:
docs/host-run-usage.md:31:## `host_run`
docs/host-run-usage.md:32:
docs/host-run-usage.md:33:```
docs/host-run-usage.md:34:lattice host_run --host <codex|claude> --agentType <type> \
docs/host-run-usage.md:35:  [--storyId B-xxxx] [--phase DEV] \
docs/host-run-usage.md:36:  ( --prompt "<text>" | --promptFile <path> ) \
docs/host-run-usage.md:37:  [--reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-001] [--lane <reviewer-lane>] \
docs/host-run-usage.md:38:  [--timeoutMs <ms>] [--deadlineMs <ms>] [--detach] \
docs/host-run-usage.md:39:  [--json]
docs/host-run-usage.md:40:```
docs/host-run-usage.md:41:
docs/host-run-usage.md:42:`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with
docs/host-run-usage.md:43:`runId/state/generation/deadlineAt`. Foreground mode submits the same durable
docs/host-run-usage.md:44:run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:
docs/host-run-usage.md:45:
docs/host-run-usage.md:46:```bash
docs/host-run-usage.md:47:lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":4,"afterSequence":12,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
docs/host-run-usage.md:48:lattice host_run_cancel '{"runId":"<runId>","reason":"operator cancelled"}'
docs/host-run-usage.md:49:```
docs/host-run-usage.md:50:
docs/host-run-usage.md:51:`waitMs` is capped at 30 seconds. A bounded return means “wake the caller and
docs/host-run-usage.md:52:inspect the current snapshot”, not “the provider failed”. Completion is known
docs/host-run-usage.md:53:only from `state=completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out` plus the terminal
docs/host-run-usage.md:54:receipt. Provider-output silence and a stale output timestamp are diagnostics,
docs/host-run-usage.md:55:never terminal predicates and never automatic-restart authorization. The
docs/host-run-usage.md:56:absolute deadline prevents permanent waiting; the next status/cancel/attach
docs/host-run-usage.md:57:touch reconciles an overdue run to terminal truth and records whether process
docs/host-run-usage.md:58:cleanup made replacement safe.
docs/host-run-usage.md:59:
docs/host-run-usage.md:60:The host subprocess executes in the **resolved project root** (the `--root`
docs/host-run-usage.md:61:target — the same root the usage-ledger rows are attributed to), independent of
docs/host-run-usage.md:62:the caller's current working directory, so where the host actually runs can
docs/host-run-usage.md:63:never diverge from where the ledger says it ran.
docs/host-run-usage.md:64:
docs/host-run-usage.md:65:Provider output is durably journaled and projected to an attached foreground
docs/host-run-usage.md:66:caller as it arrives, up to the per-run 8 MiB retention ceiling. The foreground
docs/host-run-usage.md:67:projection is explicitly bounded: once the ceiling is reached, `--json` reports
docs/host-run-usage.md:68:`truncated=true` on the `lattice.host_run.v1` result and text mode writes
docs/host-run-usage.md:69:`truncated=true` to stderr; neither promises the omitted tail.
docs/host-run-usage.md:70:`host_run_status --json` exposes the same flag as `output.truncated`. Worker
docs/host-run-usage.md:71:heartbeat and `lastProviderProgressAt` are separate:
docs/host-run-usage.md:72:the former proves only that the supervisor can update state; the latter moves
docs/host-run-usage.md:73:only when observable provider bytes arrive. `providerProgressMode=unobservable`
docs/host-run-usage.md:74:is reported honestly when progress cannot be observed. A one-line usage summary
docs/host-run-usage.md:75:is written to stderr, for example:
docs/host-run-usage.md:76:
docs/host-run-usage.md:77:```
docs/host-run-usage.md:78:usage recorded: provider=openai input=10202 cacheRead=11008 output=85 (recordId llmuse_...)
docs/host-run-usage.md:79:```
docs/host-run-usage.md:80:
docs/host-run-usage.md:81:Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
docs/host-run-usage.md:82:usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
docs/host-run-usage.md:83:capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
docs/host-run-usage.md:84:flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
docs/host-run-usage.md:85:poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
docs/host-run-usage.md:86:happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
docs/host-run-usage.md:87:retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
docs/host-run-usage.md:88:usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
docs/host-run-usage.md:89:rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
docs/host-run-usage.md:90:valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
docs/host-run-usage.md:91:later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
docs/host-run-usage.md:92:(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
docs/host-run-usage.md:93:perfectly good final usage event).
docs/host-run-usage.md:94:
docs/host-run-usage.md:95:### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)
docs/host-run-usage.md:96:
docs/host-run-usage.md:97:| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
docs/host-run-usage.md:98:|---|---|---|---|
docs/host-run-usage.md:99:| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
docs/host-run-usage.md:100:| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |
docs/host-run-usage.md:101:
docs/host-run-usage.md:102:In `--json` mode the bounded host transcript (at most 8 MiB per managed run) is
docs/host-run-usage.md:103:delivered live on **stderr** so that **stdout stays clean** for the one JSON
docs/host-run-usage.md:104:result. If the transcript exceeds that ceiling, the JSON result reports
docs/host-run-usage.md:105:`truncated=true` and does not promise the omitted tail; the JSON `stdout` field
docs/host-run-usage.md:106:carries only the bounded usage-parse tail, not an unbounded or complete
docs/host-run-usage.md:107:transcript.
docs/host-run-usage.md:108:
docs/host-run-usage.md:109:If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
docs/host-run-usage.md:110:but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
docs/host-run-usage.md:111:`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
docs/host-run-usage.md:112:`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
docs/host-run-usage.md:113:downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
docs/host-run-usage.md:114:delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
docs/host-run-usage.md:115:event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async
docs/host-run-usage.md:116:stream error too. `host_run` attaches (and, in a `finally`, removes) its own
docs/host-run-usage.md:117:stdout/stderr `'error'` listeners for the duration of the run, so a real EPIPE is
docs/host-run-usage.md:118:contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
docs/host-run-usage.md:119:once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are
docs/host-run-usage.md:120:skipped rather than risk a late unhandled `'error'`, and **every** live
docs/host-run-usage.md:121:passthrough chunk write *and* final diagnostic write is settle-aware:
docs/host-run-usage.md:122:outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
docs/host-run-usage.md:123:serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
docs/host-run-usage.md:124:by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
docs/host-run-usage.md:125:command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
docs/host-run-usage.md:126:from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
docs/host-run-usage.md:127:fires while a listener is attached.
docs/host-run-usage.md:128:
docs/host-run-usage.md:129:Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
docs/host-run-usage.md:130:runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
docs/host-run-usage.md:131:forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
docs/host-run-usage.md:132:non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
docs/host-run-usage.md:133:`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.
docs/host-run-usage.md:134:
docs/host-run-usage.md:135:### Reviewer launch
docs/host-run-usage.md:136:
docs/host-run-usage.md:137:Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
docs/host-run-usage.md:138:when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
docs/host-run-usage.md:139:registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
docs/host-run-usage.md:140:lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
docs/host-run-usage.md:141:identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
docs/host-run-usage.md:142:registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
docs/host-run-usage.md:143:in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
docs/host-run-usage.md:144:attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
docs/host-run-usage.md:145:process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.
docs/host-run-usage.md:146:
docs/host-run-usage.md:147:An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
docs/host-run-usage.md:148:`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
docs/host-run-usage.md:149:review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
docs/host-run-usage.md:150:the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
docs/host-run-usage.md:151:direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
docs/host-run-usage.md:152:below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
docs/host-run-usage.md:153:capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
docs/host-run-usage.md:154:registered broker set.
docs/host-run-usage.md:155:
docs/host-run-usage.md:156:The attestation nonce is atomically consumed once to prevent replay. That local
docs/host-run-usage.md:157:ledger is replay protection, not a same-UID security boundary. Likewise process
docs/host-run-usage.md:158:ancestry is corroboration rather than required authority: an unavailable `ps`
docs/host-run-usage.md:159:view does not reject a valid broker attestation, but any observable mixed
docs/host-run-usage.md:160:Codex/Claude ancestry rejects direct evidence even when the nearest provider
docs/host-run-usage.md:161:matches. A same-UID/root attacker that can replace trusted configuration or
docs/host-run-usage.md:162:instrument the broker is outside this local assurance boundary.
docs/host-run-usage.md:163:
docs/host-run-usage.md:164:Reviewer Prompt 不应由调用方手工拼接或假定某个 rollout mode。先由
docs/host-run-usage.md:165:`review_run_start` 按当前 Story、lane 和 `promptEnvelope.roles` 的逐角色 flag
docs/host-run-usage.md:166:选择可信正文与 full/incremental context，再让 `host_run --managedReview`
docs/host-run-usage.md:167:按 `reviewRunId` 重新取得并校验这份内容。当前可独立启用 `lattice-review-concept`、
docs/host-run-usage.md:168:`lattice-review-quality`、`lattice-review-test-coverage`、
docs/host-run-usage.md:169:`lattice-review-behavior`、`lattice-review-docs`；未启用角色保持
docs/host-run-usage.md:170:`legacy-full-context`，retired channel 不可进入该 rollout。
docs/host-run-usage.md:171:
docs/host-run-usage.md:172:ReviewRun 摘要会记录 rollout mode、role-body/context/assembled digest、selection
docs/host-run-usage.md:173:reason 和预算判定。reviewer 如发现增量材料不足，必须通过既有 escalation
docs/host-run-usage.md:174:reason 请求 full context；feature flag 本身不会授予 incremental eligibility，
docs/host-run-usage.md:175:也不会改变 pass/finding 的签名与 freshness 门禁。在途 legacy pass 仍只按其
docs/host-run-usage.md:176:原始 ReviewRun/round/Envelope 解释，不能因后来切换 flag 被重新绑定。
docs/host-run-usage.md:177:
docs/host-run-usage.md:178:```bash
docs/host-run-usage.md:179:# 1. Controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
docs/host-run-usage.md:180:lattice review_run_start '{"storyId":"B-xxxx","agent":"lattice-review-quality"}'
docs/host-run-usage.md:181:
docs/host-run-usage.md:182:# 2. Submit the exact provider reviewer; raw `bash + codex exec` is unmanaged.
docs/host-run-usage.md:183:lattice host_run '{"host":"codex","storyId":"B-xxxx","agentType":"lattice-review-quality","reviewRunId":"B-xxxx:RR-001","lane":"lattice-review-quality","managedReview":true,"detach":true,"json":true}'
docs/host-run-usage.md:184:
docs/host-run-usage.md:185:# 3. Repeat this bounded status call. Silence does not cause replacement.
docs/host-run-usage.md:186:lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":<generation>,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
docs/host-run-usage.md:187:
docs/host-run-usage.md:188:# 4. Import only after completed + replacementSafe=true + reaped=true + residualProcessGroup=false.
docs/host-run-usage.md:189:lattice managed_review_evidence_import '{"runId":"<runId>","receiptId":"<receiptId>"}'
docs/host-run-usage.md:190:```
docs/host-run-usage.md:191:
docs/host-run-usage.md:192:Inside the provider process, the managed prompt forbids `review_run_start`,
docs/host-run-usage.md:193:`review_pass_set` and `finding_add`. Its final assistant result must be exactly
docs/host-run-usage.md:194:one bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope containing
docs/host-run-usage.md:195:pass-or-findings plus truthful read evidence. After a successful provider exit,
docs/host-run-usage.md:196:the managed adapter selects only Codex's terminal `item.completed`
docs/host-run-usage.md:197:`agent_message` or Claude's terminal `result`; tool logs, arbitrary streamed
docs/host-run-usage.md:198:stdout and controller fields are ignored. The worker validates the sealed
docs/host-run-usage.md:199:story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple and atomically writes the immutable proposal.
docs/host-run-usage.md:200:Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized envelopes fail the run closed. The
docs/host-run-usage.md:201:`pass` form requires a non-empty note and no findings (an empty findings array is
docs/host-run-usage.md:202:equivalent to absence). The `findings` form requires at least one fully valid
docs/host-run-usage.md:203:finding and may carry a non-empty explanatory note; that note is diagnostic
docs/host-run-usage.md:204:only and is discarded before the immutable evidence proposal is written, so it
docs/host-run-usage.md:205:can never become a formal finding or evidence field. The older
docs/host-run-usage.md:206:descriptor-authorized `managed_review_proposal_set` command remains a
docs/host-run-usage.md:207:compatibility path, not the formal happy path; its private signing key is never
docs/host-run-usage.md:208:placed in the prompt, argv, provider environment, or durable run artifact.
docs/host-run-usage.md:209:Raw same-UID CLI calls, copied environment variables, stale PGIDs,
docs/host-run-usage.md:210:terminal/reaped runs, and ambiguous/multiple run candidates fail closed.
docs/host-run-usage.md:211:Successful terminal creation seals the proposal and journal. That state alone
docs/host-run-usage.md:212:is not importable: the receipt must also prove `replacementSafe=true`,
docs/host-run-usage.md:213:`processCleanup.reaped=true`, and
docs/host-run-usage.md:214:`processCleanup.residualProcessGroup=false`. The importer accepts only
docs/host-run-usage.md:215:`runId + receiptId`, exposes no verdict override, and preserves the provider
docs/host-run-usage.md:216:lane/ReviewRun/provenance. Both import time and the REVIEW gate revalidate the
docs/host-run-usage.md:217:same shared Proof Admissibility contract. Raw CLI stdout,
docs/host-run-usage.md:218:usage rows and time-window correlations cannot satisfy this evidence class.
docs/host-run-usage.md:219:
docs/host-run-usage.md:220:For a managed Claude reviewer, the worker materializes the authoritative prompt
docs/host-run-usage.md:221:as a mode-`0600` one-shot file below the provider's exact working directory at
docs/host-run-usage.md:222:`.lattice/runtime/host-run-prompts/`; Claude's workspace sandbox can therefore
docs/host-run-usage.md:223:read it without exposing prompt text in argv. Because a detached reviewer has no
docs/host-run-usage.md:224:interactive terminal on which to approve required inspection and Lattice CLI
docs/host-run-usage.md:225:commands, only the signed `managed_reviewer` launch profile adds Claude's
docs/host-run-usage.md:226:`--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. That same profile supplies a bounded,
docs/host-run-usage.md:227:non-secret `--json-schema` which fixes the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun
docs/host-run-usage.md:228:tuple and proposal vocabulary. The schema is an unavoidable CLI argument, but
docs/host-run-usage.md:229:contains neither prompt/capability bytes nor a controller-authored conclusion.
docs/host-run-usage.md:230:The adapter consumes only a `type=result` event with `subtype=success` and a
docs/host-run-usage.md:231:present provider-validated `structured_output`. Every other Claude result
docs/host-run-usage.md:232:event is ignored, including error/non-success envelopes and success events
docs/host-run-usage.md:233:without `structured_output`. Ordinary prose, Markdown-fenced JSON, and
docs/host-run-usage.md:234:`event.result` are never proposal inputs. Ordinary Claude `host_run` keeps its
docs/host-run-usage.md:235:configured permission policy and has no JSON schema, while Codex keeps stdin
docs/host-run-usage.md:236:transport. The private leaf is removed when the provider settles. Missing,
docs/host-run-usage.md:237:prose-only, malformed, multiple, or oversized proposal envelopes still fail
docs/host-run-usage.md:238:closed.
